verdict.rationale: Weave's `@weave.op()` tracing automatically captures inputs, outputs and execution metadata for LLM calls, building a trace tree. For supported integrations such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere and Mistral, it records token usage per call and shows it in the trace tree and calls table. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that latency/duration is captured (only implied by "execution metadata"), and independent or hands-on corroboration beyond first-party docs and the repo.

support.subject: As a developer, I can capture traces of my LLM calls with inputs, outputs, latency, and token usage

citations.quote: Weave automatically captures its code, inputs, outputs, and execution metadata.
Decorate all the functions you want to trace, this will generate a trace tree of the inputs and outputs of all your functions
When you call weave.init() and use a supported LLM integration such as OpenAI, Anthropic, Cohere, or Mistral, Weave automatically records token usage and calculates cost for each call.
Costs appear in the trace tree and in the calls table in the Weave UI.
You can trace any function using `weave.op` - from api calls to OpenAI, Anthropic, Google AI Studio etc
